patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "symbotic", 2026-09-13

profile_text.body:
Symbotic Inc. describes itself as a provider of end-to-end warehouse automation for retailers and distributors, built around robotic systems and AI software. According to the company, its systems are designed to increase facility capacity through dense storage, raise throughput, and extend efficiency gains across the supply chain with software it says sees beyond the warehouse walls. The company states that its solutions can be adapted to palletized goods, small quantity fulfillment, and omnichannel operations, and that goods ranging from 1 lb (0.5 kg) and 2 x 6.4 x 5 in (5.1 x 16.3 x 12.7 cm) up to 60 lb (27.2 kg) and 36 x 24 x 16.2 in (91.4 x 61 x 41.2 cm) can be managed and fulfilled in their native packaging, with options for loose items and cold chain requirements.

Symbotic positions itself against typical integrators, which it says are limited by their portfolio of technology partnerships and cannot resolve problems when those technologies misalign. It describes its own offering as complete, turnkey-ready, and end-to-end, with the company acting as the software and key robotic innovator for each solution. It also describes itself as a leader in industrial automation and in technology at large, and states that its purpose is to get the right goods to people who need them when they need them.

The company is a public company headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts, trading under the ticker SYM, with SEC CIK 0001837240. Its recorded litigation exposure is concentrated in Massachusetts, where 97 cases are counted.
